name: Bupropion

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Weak dopamine and noradrenaline reuptake blocker

what.text: Bupropion is an antidepressant of the aminoketone class. As Wellbutrin SR and Wellbutrin XL it is approved for depression, and Wellbutrin XL also for preventing seasonal affective disorder. It was approved for quitting smoking as Zyban. For weight, it is approved only in one tablet with naltrexone, sold as Contrave in the US and Mysimba in the EU and UK.
How it acts, according to the FDA labels

items.text: The label says the mechanism is unknown but is thought to involve noradrenaline and dopamine. Bupropion is a relatively weak blocker of their reuptake. It does not block serotonin reuptake or inhibit monoamine oxidase.

With naltrexone, lab and animal studies suggest effects on the appetite centre (hypothalamus) and the reward system. The Contrave label says the exact effects that lead to weight loss are not fully understood.

research.text: Bupropion alone was tested for weight loss in randomized trials around 2002, but was never approved for that use. It was later developed with naltrexone, which led to Contrave.

research.title: Bupropion SR for weight, 327 adults, 24 to 48 weeks (Anderson et al.)

facts.v: multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial: placebo, bupropion SR 300 or 400 mg/day; placebo group switched to bupropion after week 24
327 obese adults counselled on diet, meal replacements and exercise
24 weeks, then a 24-week extension
percent weight loss in people who completed 24 weeks

research.found: Of 327 people, 227 completed 24 weeks. Among them, weight fell 5.0% on placebo, 7.2% on 300 mg and 10.1% on 400 mg. Pulse and blood pressure changes did not differ from placebo. The analysis covered completers only.

src.label: Anderson JW, et al. Obes Res 2002

research.title: Bupropion SR in obese adults with depressive symptoms, 384 adults, 26 weeks (Jain et al.)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with a 500 kcal/day calorie-deficit diet
384 obese adults (BMI 30 to 44) with depressive symptoms but not major depression
26 weeks
weight change; depressive symptoms

research.found: Weight fell 4.6% on bupropion and 1.8% on placebo. 40% vs 16% lost at least 5%. Mood improvement did not differ between groups overall.

src.label: Jain AK, et al. Obes Res 2002

research.title: Bupropion alone, naltrexone alone or both, 419 adults (Greenway et al.)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo- and single-drug-controlled, dose-finding trial
419 adults with uncomplicated obesity
24 weeks, with a 24-week extension
percent weight change at week 24

research.found: The combinations lowered weight 3.5% to 4.7% more than placebo. The highest naltrexone combination did not differ significantly from bupropion alone; the others did.

src.label: Greenway FL, et al. J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2009

research.title: The 4 COR trials in the Contrave label, 4,536 adults

facts.v: 4 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials
4,536 adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition; 83% women
56 weeks
percent weight change; share losing at least 5%

research.found: Mean weight change on Contrave vs placebo ranged from -3.7% vs -1.7% (type 2 diabetes) to -8.1% vs -4.9% (with intensive behaviour therapy). About 45% left before week 56.

research.title: Heart safety of naltrexone plus bupropion, 8,910 adults (LIGHT)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (NCT01601704)
8,910 overweight or obese adults at higher heart risk
stopped early
heart attack, stroke or heart death

research.found: The trial ended early after the sponsor released confidential interim data. The authors said heart safety remains uncertain.

us.text: Bupropion is FDA approved, by prescription, for depression and seasonal affective disorder (Wellbutrin SR, Wellbutrin XL) and was approved for smoking cessation (Zyban). For weight, the only approved product is Contrave, with naltrexone. Using bupropion alone for weight is off-label. It has a boxed warning for suicidal thoughts. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: Wellbutrin tablets were approved December 30, 1985 as a new molecular entity (NDA 018644, now discontinued). Wellbutrin SR followed October 4, 1996 (NDA 020358) and Wellbutrin XL August 28, 2003 (NDA 021515).
Zyban, bupropion for smoking cessation, was approved May 14, 1997 (NDA 020711). FDA's data list it as discontinued.
Contrave (naltrexone and bupropion) was approved September 10, 2014 (NDA 200063) for long-term weight management. Its label says it must not be combined with other bupropion products.

antidepressants raised the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviour in children, teens and young adults in short-term trials. The labels call for close watching for worsening mood and suicidal thoughts at any age.
bupropion alone is not approved for weight loss. Using it that way is off-label.
bupropion is not a controlled substance; it does not appear on DEA's list.

world.lead: Bupropion is an approved prescription medicine in the US, Canada, the UK, the EU and Australia, and the naltrexone and bupropion combination for weight is approved in all five. WADA does not prohibit it but monitors it in competition.

after.text: European Union: in March 2025 EMA found the benefits of Mysimba still outweigh its risks for up to 12 months, called heart safety beyond that uncertain, and required a heart outcomes study with results expected in 2028.
United Kingdom: in 2020 the MHRA warned that bupropion can cause serotonin syndrome, especially in overdose or with other drugs that raise serotonin, such as SSRIs and SNRIs.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Bupropion is not prohibited. WADA's 2026 List says it is in the Monitoring Program and is not considered a prohibited substance. It stays in the 2027 Monitoring Program, in competition only.

side.text: Bupropion has a boxed warning for suicidal thoughts and behaviours. It can cause seizures, the risk rising with dose, and raise blood pressure. Common effects include dry mouth, nausea, insomnia and anxiety.

items.text: bupropion can cause seizures; the risk rises with dose. It must not be used with a seizure disorder, an eating disorder such as bulimia or anorexia, or during sudden withdrawal from alcohol, benzodiazepines, barbiturates or anti-seizure drugs. In Contrave trials, seizures occurred in about 0.1%.
it can raise blood pressure and cause hypertension.
postmarketing reports in people using it to quit smoking included mood changes, psychosis, hallucinations, paranoia, aggression, anxiety, panic, suicidal thoughts and suicide.
dry mouth, nausea, insomnia, dizziness, sore throat, belly pain, agitation, anxiety, tremor, palpitations, sweating, ringing in the ears, muscle pain, loss of appetite, frequent urination and rash.
in depression trials, 14% to 19% on bupropion SR lost more than 5 lbs, vs 6% on placebo.
must not be used with MAO inhibitors, or within 14 days of one.
the UK MHRA has warned of serotonin syndrome with other serotonergic drugs.
